attributes.additional_details: A name can save a life. Type 1 is still confused with Type 2, and misdiagnosis can mean insulin is delayed or not given, putting people at risk of life-threatening DKA. NICE specifically warns of this risk. Calling Type 1 “Banting’s” would clearly separate it from Type 2, helping medical professionals recognise that these are different diseases and helping the public understand that Type 1 is not caused by lifestyle. Please support this change and help make Type 1 harder to misunderstand.
attributes.background: For the UK Government to work with NHS bodies, medical organisations, and international diabetes organisations to recognise “Banting’s disease” as an alternative name for Type 1 diabetes in honour of Sir Frederick Banting and the discovery of insulin. To help battle misdiagnosis and negative stigma.

rejection.details: Medical terminology and clinical classification are matters for organisations such as the NHS, NICE, professional medical bodies and international health organisations rather than the UK Government.
